Ahluwalia Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:4050 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 2 nd Of February, 2026 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 15 of 2024 Aekesh Tyagi And Others Versus The State Of Mp Through Shri Anil Pratap Singh Parihar And Others Appearance: Shri Ayush Chourasia - Advocate for the appellants. Shri C.P. Singh - Government Advocate for the State. Order This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against order dated 23/07/2024 passed by Third District Judge, Morena, District Morena/Appellate Tribunal in MCA No.115/2022 as well as order dated 11/04/2022 passed by Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate, Morena in Case No.36/20/Food Safety.
texts.facts: Order This miscellaneous second appeal under Section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against order dated 23/07/2024 passed by Third District Judge, Morena, District Morena/Appellate Tribunal in MCA No.115/2022 as well as order dated 11/04/2022 passed by Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate, Morena in Case No.36/20/Food Safety. 2. Facts necessary for disposal of present appeal, in short, are that on 28/08/2019 at about 06:30 PM, Food Safety Officer alongwith his team visited the house of appellant No.1- Aekesh Tyagi because they had received an information that appellant No.1 Aekesh Tyagi and his uncle Vrindawan Tyagi- appellant No.2 are engaged in the business of adulterated milk. The police party was also accompanied by other officers and police. It was informed by police officer that both the appellants have run away from the spot. One can of 20 litres containing hydrogen peroxide, two opened tins containing 15 litres of refined oil, four blue- coloured empty milk cans were found kept at the door of the house of appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4050 2 MSA-15-2024 No.1, whereas three tins of refined palm oil, which were in sealed condition, were found hidden in wheat husk. The house of appellant No.2 is situated near to the house of appellant No.1, and behind the house of appellant No.2 one stove was constructed over which the utensil was kept, six tins of refined palm oil, which were kept in a hidden condition in the bushes, were seized. Aekesh Tyagi vs The State Of Mp Through Shri Anil Pratap ... on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112853731/ 1 An information was also received that appellant No.1 had also hidden certain articles in the field of Ram Ratan Tyagi and, accordingly, 13 tins of refined palm oil were seized from the field of Ram Ratan situated on the backside of his house, whereas 10 tins of refined palm oil were seized from the field of Ram Ratan which was situated in front of his house. In all, 32 tins of refined oil of the same batch number and manufactured by the same company were seized. Sampling was done, and the seized articles were sent to the Food Analyst. The refined palm oil was found to be an adulterant under Section 3 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Accordingly, notices were issued to appellants and other persons. Since the appellants and other noticees did not pray for re-testing of seized articles, therefore, a complaint was filed. 3. The appellants as well as other noticees filed their written statement. The evidence of Anil Pratap Singh Parihar, the Food Safety Officer was recorded. The evidence of appellant No.1, Deen Dayal Tyagi and Anil Tyagi were also recorded. Thereafter, the Adjudicating Authority found that appellants are guilty of violating the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, and accordingly, appellants and other persons were hold guilty of violating Sections 57 and 58 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Rule 26(2)(ii)(v) of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. Accordingly, for violating Section 57 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/- and for violating Section 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4050 3 MSA-15-2024 2006, a penalty of Rs.2,00,000/- in all a total penalty of Rs.4,00,000/- on appellant No.1, and similarly, the similar penalties were also imposed on appellant No.2 as well as other noticees namely, Deen Dayal Tyagi and Banti Tyagi. 4. Appellants as well as Deen Dayal Tyagi and Banti Tyagi filed their appeal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
texts.arguments: 5. Challenging the order passed by Appellate Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for appellants that there is nothing on record to suggest that seized articles were seized from the places which were in possession of appellants.
